children: Western Australia is on track to produce 1 million metric tons more wheat than expected a month ago, an industry body said on Friday, adding that the state's barley and canola harvests would also be bigger than it previously thought.
Australia is one of the world's biggest suppliers of wheat, barley and canola, and Western Australia is the country's largest crop export region.

The Grain Industry Association of Western Australia (GIWA) said in a monthly crop report the state was on track to reap 10 million tons of wheat, 6.6 million tons of barley and 4.8 million tons of canola.
A month ago, GIWA forecast production of 9 million tons of wheat, 6.1 million tons of barley and 4.3 million tons of canola.

"Without the eleventh-hour rain at the end of August, we were looking at a very ordinary year as far as production goes. We are now going into harvest in many areas with reasonable grain yield prospects," GIWA said in its report.
Harvesting happens in the final quarter of the year.
